chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who bought a ram, then it was lost from him. He said: He should buy another in its place. I said: If he bought another in its place and then found the first? He said: If both of them are still present, then he should slaughter the first and sell the latter; and if he wishes, he may slaughter it. And if he had already slaughtered the latter, he should slaughter the first along with it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The slaughter of the first only becomes obligatory upon him, when he has slaughtered the latter, if he had already marked the first sacrificial animal. But if he had not marked it, then that is not binding upon him. What indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.أَشْعَرَ: marked the sacrificial animal as designated for offering
key_terms.فَلْيَذْبَحِ: then he should slaughter it as the required sacrifice
key_terms.كَبْشًا: a ram purchased as the sacrificial animal
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ آخَرَ: another animal bought in its place as a replacement
key_terms.يَلْزَمُهُ: it becomes binding upon him as a legal obligation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a lost hajj sacrificial animal is replaced and then the original is found?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a sacrificial animal designated for hajj that becomes lost, prompting the purchase of a replacement. It explains what should be done if the original animal is later found, and includes a juristic clarification that the obligation concerning the original depends on whether it had already been marked as a sacrificial offering.
